title: Phase 7: review-packet-fixes
hook: Every `RV` row of the audit is closed: twelve are fixed in the review packet's documents and one carries a recorded reason for no change. The depth alias no longer reads as a way to skip a review with no opt-in, and each repeated rule lives in one file.
recent: Fixed twelve RV rows in the review packet and recorded no change for one
what: You can read `SKILL.md` and learn that `lite` applies the M-2 skip only when the threshold variable is set. The `Rule sources:` bullet in the review core names the separators the checker splits on, and `SKILL.md` lists the same three forbidden prefixes. `SKILL.md` says why the packet holds the `Write` tool and names the registry note. The M-1 gate is specified once, in `references/pr-state-dedup.md`, and section 8.1 summarises it. The instance-only opt-out lives in the fix-completeness checklist and the reach rule in the review core, with a link from each entry document. Section 2 of `ROUTER.md` points to the block in section 3, and two on-demand keywords no document explained are gone. Five checklists call the quick reference an entry index. `SKILL.md` and the README name the playbook package validator. The fix-completeness checklist has its divider. The packet is at version 1.9.17.0.

how: Each cited line was read and each edit was designed as literal text. Twenty-three briefs went to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at max thinking through cli-pi, in three chains of one file each and ten single-file dispatches, and every diff was read. The orchestrating session ran each task's verify command, the copy canary and its test, the drift guards, the playbook validators, the document validator on the changed files and the setup battery. The commit gate asked for a version raise on eleven changed documents, which `frontmatter-version.mjs bump` applied. The code landed as `1dca9e88ad`.
decisions: One commit for the phase, not one for each row
The operator's commit policy for this packet is one code commit for each phase. The edge case in `spec.md` assumed one commit for each task
RV-03 adds a sentence and leaves the frontmatter line alone
A comment inside the `allowed-tools` line is not safe for every frontmatter parser. The sentence sits under the Extension Floors, beside the floor that states the same limit
RV-04 keeps the skip line in `SKILL.md`
The final-line contract in section 3 points to section 8 for the skip output, and the canary pins the status string in both files
RV-06 keeps one sentence in each entry document
`SKILL.md` ties the reach to the `Case:` line of the report, which the review core does not state. The rule text and its exceptions are in the review core only
No document, playbook scenario or benchmark prompt in the hub uses them, so nothing explains or tests them. The eight other keywords stay
Decision D2 forbids a script split, and a split of a reference or the playbook index changes the router, the canary pins and the playbook gold
Lines 18 to 21 can hold one divider. The frontmatter close is on line 13. The row's evidence uses lines 19 and 21 and the asset validator
The version rose to 1.9.17.0, a patch step
The phase changes wording and removes two unused keywords. No rule, floor or status line changed

limits:
1. **`node --test` on the packet's test folder runs no test.** The folder holds one shell test, `check-rule-copies.test.sh`, so the command in REQ-002 exits 0 with a count of 0. The shell test and the canary were run beside it.
2. **A playbook row names the wrong gate.** `manual-testing-playbook/efficiency-and-restraint/minimum-evidence-gate.md` line 179 calls `references/pr-state-dedup.md` the gate the depth alias maps `lite` onto. `lite` maps onto M-2. No ledger row names this, so the line is unchanged.
3. **The wording choices have one reader.** The summary sentences that replaced the repeated rules were designed by the orchestrating session and checked against the source files. No second reader reviewed them.
